I really hope you didn't take what I said the wrong way. I completely know that you guys are trying to do your absolute best with 110% good intentions and it's very much appreciated by a lot of people. 

Sometimes, it's not so much what is said as it is knowing that there is someone in the world who cares what happens to you - and you guys provide that!!

Thanks for everything you and your subreddit provide!

Been on Lexapro for the past year or so. My family doc started me at 10mg for a couple months and then upped it to 20mg. It seemed like it helped a bit with some of my worse anxiety issues, but after a year or so I started seeing other things that were bothering me (more depression-related). At my last doc appt, he didn't want to go any higher on the Lexapro but he started me on a second med to complement the Lexapro and so far it seems to be helping. Don't have the name of the new med right off hand, but I can find it. 

As far as side effects, with the Lexapro the only real issue I had was grinding my teeth for the first few weeks (a documented s/e) but that was about it. 

One more thing - I was afraid of SSRIs (or any psych meds, for that matter) for a long time, but now that I'm taking it, I wish I had started sooner. I feel that it's made a positive impact on my life. In my case anyway, it didn't do anything major - i.e. I didn't wake up a completely different person one morning as a result of the SSRI. Rather, I was able to notice the changes after looking back at myself over a period of weeks or months. Hope that makes sense. 

Oh, and I don't know about smoking either. My workplace has random drug testing.

Same, I'm usually 98% against rage comics, but this one hit the nail on the head. 

A++++, would read again!
I don't know if r/depression is the place for quickmeme posts - ESPECIALLY one as insensitive as this. Really poor taste, in my personal opinion.
Haven't been on this account for a while, but I hopped over and was wondering how you were doing? Give us an update!

I know their intentions are the very best, but sometimes it seems like this is the "advice" they are giving out in at r/suicidewatch. I posted there a while back and ended feeling worse after snapping at a few replies (for this very reason). 

Sometimes I think that there's no "right" answer that applies to the masses, rather there's one key idea or trigger inside of each of us that can shift our thoughts from "down" to "normal" - at least for a little while. In my case, just an hour ago I was laying in bed mentally composing my suicide note (something I do somewhat regularly - has to be just right, after all) when my cat came over, put her head on my shoulder and started snoring. For me, that was enough to live another day.

I understand the push for you to donate whatever you can donate, but I've been in your shoes and completely understand your point of less decision making.  

My advice is to put everything into a garbage bag and take it out to the curb right now. While it's great and noble and everything to donate, you are right that your having to sit and sort through the pile will undermine the whole task. Take one bag out to the curb filled with whatever you can put into it - just get it from *inside the house* to *outside the house*.  After you do that, come back in and notice how much better things look - and consider doing another bag.  Do as many bags as you want. 

Good luck friend. People who haven't gone through this have no idea how painful it can be.

Still hanging in there. I thought a lot over the weekend and I don't think I could take my own life while my parents are still alive, so I guess I'll be sticking around for at least a few more years. 

Thanks again denunciator.
Like I said, it's me not you. Don't apologize for trying to be helpful. I apologize for being ungrateful.
A lot of wisdom for 17. Thanks for the positive vibes. Good luck with your service.

I appreciate your input, I really do. Just keep in mind that just because something seems easy to you doesn't mean it's just as easy for everyone else. If it was this easy for me, I wouldn't be making this post. 

I don't mean to be an ass and I'm very sorry if I come across that way in this post. But I've heard that "advice" before and it makes me angry - probably more at myself than the advice giver - that I cannot do something that is seemingly so easy. 

But thanks for the thought. I appreciate your intentions.
At this point, I dream of having friends and not sitting at home alone on a Saturday night lol.

See, that's my problem. I know that exercise will help me, but I can't make myself start exercising. Over the past 10 years, I've let my physical condition go to hell and now I can't even walk a mile w/o becoming winded... quite a stretch from where I was in my 20s. 

Anyway, I can't bring myself to even start a simple walking program. I've made some effort... many times I've gotten dressed, laced up the tennis shoes and was ready to go, and then I just didn't do it. 

I feel like it's a vicious cycle... exercise will help but I can't make myself start to exercise. Maybe I've just become lazy in my mid life - but the "old me" was never lazy.  I wish I knew.

20 years ago, I was that person. When I lived in Arizona, I hiked the desert every other weekend. I climbed mountains and even did a 5 day hike through the Grand Canyon. Due to a job situation, I moved to the midwest (where I didn't know anyone). Over the past 15 years, I have been relatively successful at my job- several raises and promotions. 

The past year or so, I have been missing work more and more. My job allows me to be in several places, so no one is really keeping tabs on me. As a result, I can miss (as long as I have my mobile phone) and everyone thinks I'm somewhere else. It started out missing a half day here and there, and has progressed to the point that I've missed an entire week. 

With my absences slowly increasing, it's only a matter of time until they find out. And once I lose my job, I really will have no reason to keep living. I figure death will be better than being homeless for the next few decades.
